title: exercise_attempt
description: One graded answer to a COURSEWARE question — a lesson exercise, a topic-test item, a placement probe item, a drill item or an exam item. APPEND-ONLY: never updated, never deleted. This is the mistake index's source table (design/assessment.md §4.3) and it is deliberately NOT review_log: an exercise answer never writes a review_log row and never mutates a card's scheduling fields (§4.2), because review_log is the FSRS optimizer's only training set and an exercise answer is binary, usually not due, and targets 1..n items rather than one card. RUNTIME class: minted per learner, never committed to this repo.

x-yomineko.note: item_refs is COPIED from the question as served, not read through it at query time. The courseware is versioned and a repaired exercise may retarget; a mistake index that re-reads today's refs would rewrite what the learner was actually asked. The copy is bounded (median 1 entry) and it is what makes the index replayable. The mistake_index is a VIEW over this entity (WEAKNESS_V1, design/assessment.md §4.3; reference implementation in scripts/validate/test_assessment_fixtures.py), never a table.

attempt_id.description: `xat:<opaque>`. Opaque and unordered on purpose — ordering belongs to answered_at, not to a key.

question.description: The question as served, by stable id: `ex:` for a lesson or topic-test exercise, an exam-bank item id, a `conj:`/`role:` drill item id.

question_form.description: The form actually shown. Stored so a miss rate can be split by form — missing a production item and missing a 4-option recognition item are not the same evidence. Vocabulary owner: design — design/lesson_schema.md ('Exercise records', the ten `type` values).

item_refs.description: The question's item_refs AS SERVED, copied not referenced (see x-yomineko.note). Same entry shape as common#/$defs/ItemRef minus derived_by. Empty only for a question that legitimately targets no corpus item — the pre-N5 method items in course/item_ref_exemptions.json.

context.description: Which surface asked. `ref` is the lesson, the assessment attempt or the exam attempt the question was served in; null for a free practice-hub drill, which belongs to no sitting.

kind.description: Vocabulary owner: design — design/assessment.md#44-the-schema-fragment. Widening it is an edit there, never a side effect of regenerating this schema from the data.

ref.description: `les:` for a lesson, `asm:` for a topic test or a placement sitting, `att:` for an exam paper, null for a drill.

answer_given.description: What the learner submitted, as submitted. Null when the question was skipped or timed out.

graded_by.description: Where the verdict came from. Lesson exercises grade client-side today from data the SSR HTML carries; anything scored must grade server-side against a withheld key, the way the exam simulator already does. Storing it means the mistake index can exclude client verdicts if the app ever needs to. Vocabulary owner: design — design/assessment.md#44-the-schema-fragment.

client_key.description: The idempotency key the client supplied. A dropped connection during an answer must not double-count it (api_contract.md §8, 'every write is idempotent under a client-supplied key').
